venue: 2025 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
keywords: Training; Visualization; Reviews; Large language models; Gaze tracking; Transformers; Market research; Data augmentation; Question answering (information retrieval); Data models; eye-tracking; cognitive signals; natural language processing; large language models; transformers
abstract: Recently, the integration of cognitive neuroscience in Natural Language Processing (NLP) has gained significant attention. This article provides a critical and timely overview of recent advancements in leveraging cognitive signals, particularly Eyetracking (ET) signals, to enhance Language Models (LMs) and Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). By incorporating user-centric cognitive signals, these approaches address key challenges, including data scarcity and the environmental costs of training large-scale models. Cognitive signals enable efficient data augmentation, faster convergence, and improved human alignment. The review emphasises the potential of ET data in tasks like Visual Question Answering (VQA) and mitigating hallucinations in MLLMs, and concludes by discussing emerging challenges and research trends.

titulo: Distilling Wisdom: A Review on Optimizing Learning From Massive Language Models
autores: D. Zhang; D. Listiyani; P. Singh; M. Mohanty
venue: IEEE Access
keywords: Transformers; Large language models; Computational modeling; Surveys; Natural language processing; Predictive models; Artificial intelligence; Technological innovation; Encoding; Context modeling; Artificial intelligence (AI); large language model (LLM); knowledge distillation (KD); optimization
abstract: In the era of Large Language Models (LLMs), Knowledge Distillation (KD) enables the transfer of capabilities from proprietary LLMs to open-source models. This survey provides a detailed discussion of the basic principles, algorithms, and implementation methods of knowledge distillation. It explores KD’s impact on LLMs, emphasizing its utility in model compression, performance enhancement, and self-improvement. Through the analysis of practical examples such as DistilBERT, TinyBERT, and MobileBERT, the paper demonstrates how knowledge distillation can markedly enhance the efficiency and applicability of large language models in real-world scenarios. The discussion encompasses the varied applications of KD across multiple domains, including industrial systems, embedded systems, Natural Language Processing (NLP), multi-modal processing, and vertical domains, such as medicine, law, science, finance, and materials science. This survey outlines current KD methodologies and future research directions, highlighting its role in advancing AI technologies and fostering innovation across different sectors.

titulo: Survey and Evaluation of Converging Architecture in LLMs Based on Footsteps of Operations
autores: S. Kim; J. Moon; J. Oh; I. Choi; J. -S. Yang
venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Computer Society
keywords: Computer architecture; Computational modeling; Transformers; Training; Neural networks; Context modeling; Artificial intelligence; Encoding; Surveys; Optimization; Edge computing; LLM; NLP; transformer architecture; and server deployment
abstract: Large language models (LLMs), which have emerged from advances in natural language processing (NLP), enable chatbots, virtual assistants, and numerous domain-specific applications. These models, often comprising billions of parameters, leverage the Transformer architecture and Attention mechanisms to process context effectively and address long-term dependencies more efficiently than earlier approaches, such as recurrent neural networks (RNNs). Notably, since the introduction of Llama, the architectural development of LLMs has significantly converged, predominantly settling on a Transformer-based decoder-only architecture. The evolution of LLMs has been driven by advances in high-bandwidth memory, specialized accelerators, and optimized architectures, enabling models to scale to billions of parameters. However, it also introduces new challenges: meeting compute and memory efficiency requirements across diverse deployment targets, ranging from data center servers to resource-constrained edge devices. To address these challenges, we survey the evolution of LLMs at two complementary levels: architectural trends and their underlying operational mechanisms. Furthermore, we quantify how hyperparameter settings influence inference latency by profiling kernel-level execution on a modern GPU architecture. Our findings reveal that identical models can exhibit varying performance based on hyperparameter configurations and deployment contexts, emphasizing the need for scalable and efficient solutions. The insights distilled from this analysis guide the optimization of performance and efficiency within these converged LLM architectures, thereby extending their applicability across a broader range of environments.

titulo: Deep Learning in ChatGPT - A Survey
autores: A. M. J. Hashana; P. Brundha; M. U. Ahamed Ayoobkhan; F. S
venue: 2023 7th International Conference on Trends in Electronics and Informatics (ICOEI)
keywords: Deep learning; Training; Adaptation models; Computational modeling; Computer architecture; Chatbots; Transformers; Artificial Intelligence; Convolutional Neural Networks; ChatGPT; Generative Adversarial Networks; Recurrent Neural Networks
abstract: Abstract-As a subset of machine learning, deep learning makes use of multiple-layer neural networks to learn with available data and make decisions or predictions. A large language model called ChatGPT is based on deep learning, specifically a type of neural network called a transformer. ChatGPT's transformer architecture uses attention mechanisms to focus on the most important parts of the input, allowing it to process and comprehend a large amount of text data. In order for the model to comprehend the context and meaning of natural language text, it is trained on a huge database of text, including articles and books. One of the main importance of using deep learning in ChatGPT is its intelligence to understand relationships and patterns from the input text and generate or predict new text that is homogeneous to the input/training data. Because of this, ChatGPT is able to respond to questions and prompts in a manner that is comparable to that of a human, making it useful for a wide scope of natural language processing missions like translating languages, summarizing texts, and responding to questions. It's worth noting that, while deep learning has been highly effective in ChatGPT, it is not without its limitations. To train, deep learning models can be very complex and require a lot of data and computing power.

titulo: Survey of Generative Artificial Intelligence Powered Human-Data Interfaces in Big Data Systems
autores: Y. Gao; A. Roy; V. Chodnekar; C. Solur; G. Pan
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
keywords: Surveys; Privacy; Data privacy; Structured Query Language; Costs; Generative AI; Big Data; Writing; Strategic planning; Software; Big Data; Databases; Generative AI; Human-Centric Data
abstract: Accessing and making sense of data for human decision-making has become one central task in big data systems nowadays. Traditional approaches rely heavily on technologies such as SQL, proprietary and open-source reporting software, and full-text search engines. Recent advances in Gen-AI, particularly large language models, have shown strong capability to sift through massive datasets and present insights of the data in a human-readable format. However, integrating Gen-AI into big data systems can bring other issues and concerns regarding data management and model deployment. In this survey, we provide a comprehensive overview of how LLMs and related Gen-AI technologies are transforming the ways in which humans interact with and consume data from three levels in terms of various users interaction. In addition, this manuscript illustrates recent Gen-AI advancements and propose a conceptual framework of current methodologies according to scalability, adaptability, and value. This analysis also discusses benefits of applying Gen-AI in real-world environments and examines the emerging techniques behind Gen-AI-driven big data systems. Furthermore, we highlight the key challenges and tradeoffs such as cost, privacy, and latency that must be considered before establishing Gen-AI as a reliable interface for big data. We believe that this work can serve as a general guide for researchers and practitioners seeking insights to understand the evolving relationship between Gen-AI and big data ecosystems.

titulo: The Survey of Model Scale Impact on Knowledge Distillation Efficiency in LLM
autores: S. Budiman; S. Rochimah; D. O. Siahaan
venue: 2025 International Electronics Symposium (IES)
keywords: Surveys; Adaptation models; Scalability; Education; Taxonomy; Natural language processing; Safety; Reliability; Object recognition; Model compression; Knowledge distillation; scalability; compression; LLM; efficiency
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have exhibited remarkable capabilities in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks, yet their substantial memory and computational requirements pose significant challenges. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been applied to LLMs to reduce their substantial demands for memory and computation resources. This study aims to find the most efficient most efficient KD method for various scales of LLMs. This study observes the recent advances in KD methods by analyzing eleven state-of-the-art KD methods. We categorize these techniques into five groups: divergence-based, reward-based, data-based, task-specific, and hybrid methods. Each method is evaluated based on its efficacy and efficiency in distilling knowledge into smaller, more deployable models. Our findings reveal two key insights: (1) The optimal KD method is contingent upon various factors, including the LLM's scale, task characteristics, and the desired efficiency, with each approach presenting distinct trade-offs. (2) This study has evolved from simple output distribution “imitation” to sophisticated “teaching” paradigms, where context-aware mechanisms optimize knowledge transfer. This survey provides a foundation for future research by systematically outlining current approaches and their trade-offs. Furthermore, the availability of open source implementations for these KD techniques is paramount.

titulo: Towards Context-Driven Approaches to Visual Affordance Recognition : A Comprehensive Survey
autores: E. Joffroy-Frixons; Y. Mourchid; N. Ragot; Y. Ding
venue: IEEE Transactions on Cognitive and Developmental Systems
keywords: Context; Modeling; Grounding; Affordances; Signal detection; Visualization; Learning (artificial intelligence); Labeling; Measurement; Conferences; Visual affordance detection; contextual affordance; text embedding; computer vision; deep learning model
abstract: With the rise of robotics, affordance detection has become a key element for improving and strengthening human and robot object interactions. Thanks to recent progress in deep learning, affordance detection has become more precise and versatile. However, with the increasing use of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Visual Transformers (ViTs), the research focus shifted from clearly defined classes and dynamics to wider applications. Due to these new applications, context-based affordance recognition has gained popularity. However, to the best of our knowledge, there is no unified work around the comprehension and description of these advances in a context-based affordance detection. Therefore, this paper aims to review recent contributions in the field of contextual affordance detection, to provide solid foundations to the community, highlighting current works and future trends. This paper first introduces the context types and different tasks for affordance recognition. Then, various context-based methods for affordance recognition are presented, classified according to the context they are based on and their learning paradigms. Next, relevant datasets are presented with the respective methods’ performances on these datasets. Finally, this paper provides a discussion around the presented results and the trends observed through this survey, followed by a summary of the challenges and open questions to be faced in the future.

titulo: Inference Acceleration Techniques for Large AI Models: A Survey
autores: F. A. Mohamed; M. -A. Chadi; H. Mousannif
venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Innovative Research in Applied Science, Engineering and Technology (IRASET)
keywords: Modeling; Quantization (signal); Optimization; Timing; Hardware; Information rates; Printing; Throughput; Memory; Accuracy; Inference Acceleration; Acceleration Techniques; Acceleration Metrics
abstract: The rapid growth of large AI models such as large language models (LLMs), vision transformers (ViTs), and multimodal models has created a critical need for efficient inference. This survey reviews a broad spectrum of inference acceleration techniques from algorithmic and architectural methods to model compression, hardware optimizations, and system-level strategies. We discuss dynamic inference methods such as early exiting, mixture-of-experts, and adaptive attention; model compression including pruning, quantization, and weight sharing; hardwareaware optimizations including inference compilers and custom kernels; and system strategies including batching, caching, and scheduling. We compare techniques in terms of latency, throughput, memory, and accuracy trade-offs, providing useful details for practitioners. Notably, methods like aggressive quantization can yield approximately three to four times throughput improvements, knowledge distillation can speed up inference by approximately two times, and advanced schedulers can boost multi-query serving throughput by approximately two to five times. This paper serves as a reference for practitioners and researchers seeking a unified view of inference acceleration techniques.

titulo: Integrating External Knowledge with LLMs: A Systematic Review of RAG Approaches
autores: I. Mikulić; M. Vlaić; G. Delač; M. Šilić; K. Vladimir
venue: 2025 MIPRO 48th ICT and Electronics Convention
keywords: Training; Accuracy; Large language models; Pipelines; Retrieval augmented generation; Knowledge based systems; Natural language processing; Libraries; Reliability; Systematic literature review; RAG; Retrieval; IR; LLM
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in natural language understanding and generation, exhibiting exceptional in-context learning abilities without requiring extensive fine-tuning. However, these models often suffer from significant limitations, including hallucinations where fabricated or incorrect information is presented as fact, and the need for constant retraining in order to effectively integrate new knowledge. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a promising paradigm to address these challenges by combining LLMs with information retrieval (IR) techniques. By leveraging external knowledge bases, RAG pipelines retrieve and incorporate relevant information dynamically, enhancing the factual accuracy and adaptability of LLMs. This paper provides an overview of the state-of-the-art methods for implementing RAG in LLMs, examining key components of the RAG pipeline, including data preparation, retrieval, reranking, and post-retrieval techniques. We aim to highlight how these components collectively enable LLMs to achieve greater reliability and flexibility, paving the way for more robust AI applications.

titulo: Reinforcement Learning for Neural Network Compression: A Taxonomy of MDP Design, Action Spaces, Reward Engineering, and Learning Algorithms
autores: F. Baradaran; M. Raji
venue: IEEE Access
keywords: Modeling; Quantization (signal); Optimization; Learning (artificial intelligence); Reinforcement learning; Model compression; Hardware; Design methodology; Neural networks; Computer architecture; Model Compression; Reinforcement Learning (RL); Automated Model Compression; Network Pruning; Quantization
abstract: Deploying large Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) and Large Language Models (LLMs) on resource-constrained hardware remains challenging due to their high computational, memory, and energy requirements. Conventional compression techniques, including pruning, quantization, and architectural optimization, can reduce these costs effectively; however, they often rely on manually designed heuristics and rule-based strategies. Such approaches face difficulties in efficiently exploring the large search spaces of modern neural architectures, frequently leading to sub-optimal trade-offs between model accuracy and efficiency. To address these limitations, Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as an effective framework for automated model compression by formulating the optimization process as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). Although numerous RL-based compression methods have recently been proposed, existing survey studies primarily categorize the literature according to the compression type, such as pruning or quantization, while providing limited analysis of the underlying RL mechanisms and design strategies. To address this gap, this survey presents, to the best of current knowledge, the first comprehensive RL-centric taxonomy for model compression. The state-of-the-art methods are systematically analyzed across four key dimensions: (1) MDP modeling strategies, including sequential layer-wise, topology-aware, multi-agent, dynamic runtime, and efficient environment modeling formulations; (2) action space design, covering quantization-oriented, pruning-oriented, joint compression, dynamic input-adaptive, and hierarchical action spaces; (3) reward function engineering, including accuracy-oriented, compression-aware, hardware-aware, multi-objective, and task-specific reward formulations; and (4) reinforcement learning algorithms, encompassing value-based methods, actor–critic approaches, policy-gradient techniques, Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), and hybrid/model-based RL frameworks. The survey further examines recent developments ranging from pruning and mixed-precision quantization in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to token pruning, context compression, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) pruning in Vision Transformers (ViTs) and LLMs, highlighting the relationships between RL design choices and compression performance. The review also describes the literature-selection scope, summarizes representative quantitative results, and discusses key limitations affecting scalability, transferability, benchmarking, and deployment. Overall, this paper provides a structured RL-centric perspective on automated model compression, identifies current challenges and research gaps, and outlines promising directions for developing scalable, adaptive, and hardware-aware compression systems.

titulo: Auditing Demographic Bias in Mistral: An Open-Source LLM’s Diagnostic Performance on the MedQA Benchmark
autores: H. O. A. Ahmed; A. Hamid Sadka
venue: IEEE Access
keywords: Medical diagnostic imaging; Accuracy; Cognition; Medical services; Benchmark testing; Large language models; Artificial intelligence; Systematics; Safety; Robustness; Large language models (LLMs); demographic bias; fairness auditing; medical question answering; MedQA benchmark; Mistral 7B-Instruct; open-weight models; Ollama; Wilson confidence interval; statistical bias evaluation; digital health; ethical AI
abstract: The application of large language models (LLMs) within clinical decision-support frameworks is receiving growing research attention, yet their fairness and demographic robustness remain insufficiently understood. This study introduces MedQA-Demog, a purpose-built, label-invariant extension of the MedQA-USMLE benchmark, designed to enable systematic auditing of demographic bias in medical reasoning models. Using a deterministic augmentation framework, we generated 4,659 question-answer items that incorporated counterfactual variations in gender, race/ethnicity, and age, and validated them through automated integrity and balance checks. We evaluated the Mistral 7B-Instruct model under stochastic (temperature = 0.7) and deterministic (temperature = 0.0) inference rules via the Ollama local environment, applying Wilson’s 95% confidence intervals,  $\chi ^{2}/z$ -tests, McNemar’s paired analysis, and Cohen’s h effect sizes to quantify fairness. Across all demographic variants, diagnostic accuracy remained consistent ( $\Delta \lt 0.04$ ; p >0.05), and all performance gaps fell within Minimal or Low Bias thresholds. Confusion-matrix and prediction-balance analyses revealed no systematic over- or under-prediction patterns, while power analysis confirmed that observed fluctuations were below the minimum detectable effect ( $\approx 0.057$ ). A stratified robustness analysis further confirms that these fairness patterns persist across question difficulty levels and are not an artefact of uniformly limited performance. These findings demonstrate that open-weight, instruction-tuned LLMs can maintain demographic stability in clinical reasoning when evaluated through reproducible, controlled pipelines. This framework provides a practical foundation for bias evaluation in open clinical LLMs, supporting their ethical integration into digital health tools and clinical decision-support systems.

titulo: LLM-MedQA: Enhancing Medical Question Answering through Case Studies in Large Language Models
autores: H. Yang; H. Chen; H. Guo; Y. Chen; C. -S. Lin; S. Hu; J. Hu; X. Wu; X. Wang
venue: 2025 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
keywords: Measurement; Accuracy; Large language models; Decision making; Zero shot learning; Question answering (information retrieval); Data models; Cognition; Reliability; Medical diagnostic imaging; MedQA; LLMs; Llama; Zero-Shot Learning
abstract: Accurate and efficient question-answering systems are essential for high-quality patient care in the medical field. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have made remarkable strides across various domains, they still face challenges in medical question answering, particularly in understanding domain-specific terminology and performing complex reasoning, limiting their effectiveness in critical applications. To address this, we propose a multi-agent medical question-answering (MedQA) system incorporating similar case generation. We leverage the Llama3.1:70B model in a multi-agent architecture to enhance enhance zero-shot classification on the MedQA dataset, utilizing the model’s inherent medical knowledge and reasoning capabilities without additional training data. Experimental results show substantial gains over existing benchmark models, with improvements of 7% in both accuracy and F1-score across various medical QA tasks. Furthermore, we examine the model’s interpretability and reliability in addressing complex medical queries. This research not only offers a robust solution for medical question answering but also establishes a foundation for broader applications of LLMs in the medical domain.

titulo: Assessing the Performance of Large Language Models on the Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE): Insights from GPT-4 Turbo, Gemini Advanced, and LLaMA 3.1 (70B)
autores: R. M. Pattanshetti; S. Sidddanagoudra; S. Chand; P. S; R. Hebbar; Vaishnavi
venue: 2025 International Conference on Biomedical Engineering and Sustainable Healthcare (ICBMESH)
keywords: Training; Learning systems; Decision support systems; Adaptation models; Accuracy; Large language models; Medical services; Rendering (computer graphics); Internet; Biomedical engineering; Large Language Models (LLMs); Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE); Medical Licensing Examinations; GPT-4 Turbo; LLaMA 3.1 (70B); Gemini Advanced; AI in Medical Education
abstract: This study evaluates three advanced Large Language Models (LLMs)—GPT-4 Turbo, Gemini Advanced, and Meta’s LLaMA 3.1 (70B)—for accurately answering multiple-choice questions from the Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE). Using a curated set of 427 text-based questions from recent exams, the investigation assessed each model’s overall accuracy, consistency, and error distribution, with statistical validation via McNemar’s test. GPT-4 Turbo achieved roughly 93% accuracy, while Gemini Advanced and LLaMA 3.1 (70B) both approximated 87%, with no significant difference between them. High agreement among models indicates consistent decision-making and stable interpretative patterns. These findings underscore the potential of LLMs as complementary tools for exam preparation, particularly in resource-limited settings. Moreover, the results support the viability of open-source models—exemplified by Meta’s LLaMA 3.1 (70B)—in terms of cost-effectiveness and adaptability. Future research will explore diverse question formats and the integration of these models into clinical decision support systems to further enhance their role in modern medical education.

titulo: Efficient Adaptation of Large Language Models for Sentiment Classification: A Comparative Study of QLoRA, LoRA, and Full Fine-Tuning Under Resource Constraints
autores: T. Ghosh; S. A. Alex
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Distributed Computing and Electrical Circuits and Electronics (ICDCECE)
keywords: Modeling; LoRa; Training; Quantization (signal); Tuning; Accuracy; Large language models; Ranking (statistics); Graphics processing units; Printing; LLM; Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning; QLoRA; LoRA; Sentiment Analysis; Mixed Precision Training; Ablation Study; GPU Power Profiling
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) achieve state-of-the-art performance on natural language processing tasks but impose substantial computational demands that limit accessibility in academic and resource-constrained environments. This paper presents a comprehensive empirical study comparing three fine-tuning strategies—4-bit QLoRA, 16-bit LoRA, and 16-bit Full Fine-Tuning—applied to Facebook’s OPT-1.3B on the IMDb sentiment classification benchmark. Experiments are conducted with 2,500 training and 2,500 test samples, class-wise evaluation metrics, proper latency methodology with GPU synchronization (torch.cuda.synchronize), and actual power measurement via nvidia-smi. A LoRA rank ablation study ($r \in\{4,8,16\}$) further characterises the accuracy–efficiency trade-off under 4-bit quantization. Results show that 4-bit QLoRA achieves competitive accuracy with only 0.32% trainable parameters, reducing peak GPU memory by $\approx 75 \%$ relative to 16-bit Full Fine-Tuning while incurring a negligible accuracy penalty. The study provides reproducible, hardware-aware insights for deploying parameter-efficient LLMs on consumer-grade GPUs.

titulo: Soft Prompts vs LoRA: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models
autores: S. Kaza; A. M; S. S. G
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Advances in Computing Research On Science Engineering and Technology (ACROSET)
keywords: LoRa; Modeling; Training; Tuning; Timing; Unsolicited e-mail; Ranking (statistics); Fake news; Signal detection; Large language models; Large Language Models; Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning; Soft Prompts; LoRA; Low-Rank Adaptation; DistilBERT; Natural Language Processing; Text Classification
abstract: In this study, two highly efficient PEFT techniques Soft Prompts and LoRA will be examined by applying them to DistilBERT pre-trained model. The effectiveness of the chosen fine-tuning techniques will be compared through conducting experiments with three different tasks in NLP domain – fake news classification, spam detection, and sentiment analysis on Amazon Fine Food Reviews data set. In order to make the comparison more accurate, six indicators will be taken into consideration during evaluations – accuracy, F1 score, precision, recall, training, and evaluation time. According to obtained results, the LoRA technique proves its superiority over other techniques in terms of efficiency as it yields the best results both in terms of metrics and time.

titulo: LLaMA-Reviewer: Advancing Code Review Automation with Large Language Models through Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
autores: J. Lu; L. Yu; X. Li; L. Yang; C. Zuo
venue: 2023 IEEE 34th International Symposium on Software Reliability Engineering (ISSRE)
keywords: Codes; Automation; Quality assurance; Software reliability; Task analysis; Tuning; Software engineering; Code Review Automation; Large Language Models (LLMs); Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT); Deep Learning; LLaMA; Software Quality Assurance
abstract: The automation of code review activities, a long-standing pursuit in software engineering, has been primarily addressed by numerous domain-specific pre-trained models. Despite their success, these models frequently demand extensive resources for pre-training from scratch. In contrast, Large Language Models (LLMs) provide an intriguing alternative, given their remarkable capabilities when supplemented with domain-specific knowledge. However, their potential for automating code review tasks remains largely unexplored.In response to this research gap, we present LLaMA-Reviewer, an innovative framework that leverages the capabilities of LLaMA, a popular LLM, in the realm of code review. Mindful of resource constraints, this framework employs parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods, delivering high performance while using less than 1% of trainable parameters.An extensive evaluation of LLaMA-Reviewer is conducted on two diverse, publicly available datasets. Notably, even with the smallest LLaMA base model consisting of 6.7B parameters and a limited number of tuning epochs, LLaMA-Reviewer equals the performance of existing code-review-focused models.The ablation experiments provide insights into the influence of various fine-tuning process components, including input representation, instruction tuning, and different PEFT methods. To foster continuous progress in this field, the code and all PEFT-weight plugins have been made open-source.

titulo: Research on Automated Grading Methods for Handwritten Programming Assignments Based on Fine-Tuning Large Language Models
autores: D. Shi; Y. Zhan; N. Chen; N. Ma
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on Computer Science and Technologies in Education (CSTE)
keywords: Modeling; Machine learning; Tuning; Optical character recognition; Printing; Programming; Large language models; Ranking (statistics); Machining; Codes; handwritten programming assignments; automated grading; large language models; QLoRA fine-tuning
abstract: Grading handwritten programming assignments for “Algorithm Design and Analysis” is burdensome and suffers from inconsistent scores. This study analyzes the potential and challenges of using large language models (LLMs) for automated grading. It proposes a technical framework based on QLoRA for parameter-efficient fine-tuning. An empirical study systematically compares three approaches: traditional machine learning, prompt learning, and fine-tuning. Experimental results show the framework's strong robustness to OCR noise. The fine-tuned model achieves an ICC of 0.8174. It significantly outperforms traditional methods and prompt learning in scoring consistency. This work provides a highly reliable automated solution for the digital transformation of teaching.

titulo: MLX vs MPS on Apple Silicon: A Comparative Empirical Study of LoRA Fine-Tuning Performance for LLMs
autores: A. T. Kabakuş
venue: 2026 10th International Artificial Intelligence and Data Processing Symposium (IDAP)
keywords: Modeling; Training; Memory; LoRa; Timing; Tuning; Silicon; Printing; Large language models; Machine learning; large language model; fine-tuning; LoRA; Apple Silicon; MLX; MPS
abstract: Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) on Apple Silicon devices has gained increasing attention due to their unified memory architecture and integrated GPU capabilities. Two relevant software backends for this purpose are PyTorch with Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) and Apple’s native MLX framework. This paper presents a controlled empirical comparison of both backends for Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning of the TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 model on an Apple A18 Pro chip. Using a dataset of 200 prompt-response samples derived from the Alpaca Cleaned dataset, training was performed for 200 steps under matched experimental conditions, including a LoRA rank of eight, a LoRA scaling factor of 16, a dropout rate of 0.05, a learning rate of $\mathbf{1} \times \mathbf{1 0}^{-\mathbf{4}}$, three warmup steps, a maximum gradient norm of 1.0, and a maximum sequence length of 128 tokens. Experimental results show that MLX completes the training process in 52.15 s, compared with 4,809.89 s for MPS, corresponding to an approximately 92.2-fold speedup in training time. MLX achieves a throughput of 3.835 samples/s, whereas MPS achieves 0.0416 samples/s. Despite this substantial difference in execution time, both backends exhibit broadly similar loss behavior, with average losses of 1.626 for MLX and 1.759 for MPS, and final losses of 1.281 and 1.340, respectively. The observed results indicate that MLX provides substantially higher execution efficiency for the evaluated LoRA workload while exhibiting broadly similar loss dynamics to MPS. Gradient norms exhibit broadly similar magnitudes, although their variability differs between the two backends. These findings suggest that MLX can provide a substantial performance advantage over PyTorch MPS for LoRA fine-tuning on Apple Silicon under the evaluated experimental configuration, particularly in time-sensitive scenarios.

titulo: A Survey on Federated Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models
autores: Q. Wen; X. Zhang; N. Xiang; J. Chen; X. Wang; J. Zhang
venue: 2025 11th International Conference on Big Data and Information Analytics (BigDIA)
keywords: Surveys; Training; Adaptation models; Data privacy; Costs; Reviews; Federated learning; Large language models; Data models; Optimization; Federated Learning; Large Language Models; Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable efficacy across diverse domains, yet their deployment in sensitive sectors is constrained by data privacy. Federated Learning (FL) offers a promising paradigm for collaborative model training without exposing raw data, while Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) techniques substantially reduce adaptation costs. This survey systematically reviews the integration of FL and PEFT for LLMs, elucidating foundational architectures, mainstream PEFT methodologies, and federated adaptation frameworks. We analyze representative approaches, highlight open challenges, including communication bottlenecks, task and model heterogeneity, parameter anonymity, and adaptation profile misalignment, and propose future research directions. Our work aims to provide a comprehensive reference for advancing privacy-preserving, scalable, and efficient LLM fine-tuning in federated environments.

titulo: Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Telugu Sentiment Analysis Using QLoRA
autores: K. Anuradha; V. S. Solomi; S. R. Chand
venue: 2026 International Conference on Machine Learning and Autonomous Systems (ICMLAS)
keywords: Feedback; Circuits; LoRa; Radio access networks; Regional area networks; Communication systems; Internet; Protocols; HTTP; Computer networks; Low-Resource NLP; QLoRA; Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning; Code-Mixed Text
abstract: This paper presents a parameter-efficient sentiment analysis system for low-resource, code-mixed text using LLaMA 3.1 8B Instruct fine-tuned with Quantized LowRank Adaptation (QLoRA) and 4-bit NF4 quantization. We generated a balanced synthetic dataset (2,520 samples) across entertainment, reviews, and social domains to address data scarcity. Results show $\mathbf{8 0. 2} \pm \mathbf{0. 4 \%}$ accuracy (5 runs), outperforming XLM-R $(79.6 \pm 0.3 \%$, $\mathrm{p}=0.018)$. Real-world validation: ACTSA (77.3%), DravidianCodeMix (75.8%). QLoRA enables training on single consumer GPUs ($<8 ~\text{GB}$), validating efficiency for resource-constrained NLP and framework demonstrates strong generalization capability across domains and maintains balanced precision and recall despite the presence of linguistic variability, transliteration noise, and informal expressions in Telugu-English code-mixed data. The use of synthetic data combined with parameterefficient fine-tuning significantly reduces the dependency on large annotated corpora while preserving contextual understanding. Experimental analysis also confirms that lowbit quantization and adapter-based training improve memory efficiency and scalability without degrading predictive performance. These findings highlight the practicality of deploying large language model-based sentiment systems in real-world low-resource environments, supporting future multilingual NLP applications and scalable adaptation to other under-represented languages.

titulo: Knowledge Graph Enhanced Human-Aligned Evaluation of Database Design Via Parameter-Efficient Large Language Models
autores: B. Dong; P. Liu; Z. Shao; S. Dong; Y. Li
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on Data-driven Optimization of Complex Systems (DOCS)
keywords: Modeling; Design methodology; Tuning; Knowledge graphs; Databases; Printing; Large language models; LoRa; Human-AI Collaboration; Knowledge Graph; Larg e Language Model; Evidence-guided reasoning; Supervised Fine-Tuning
abstract: The evaluation of database design quality is essential for assessing undergraduate theses (projects), yet existing approaches suffer from subjective manual reviews and limited rule representation, leading to inconsistent evaluations. This paper proposes a structured evidence-driven framework with expert preference alignment for database design quality assessment. The method constructs knowledge graphs of student and standard designs to generate structured evidence, which is combined with database design information to guide parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms text-only and non-fine-tuned baselines on MAE, Pearson, and Acc@1 metrics. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of knowledge graph enhancement and parameter-efficient fine-tuning.

titulo: EvoAPR: Enhancing Large Language Models for Automatic Program Repair with Genetic Algorithm and Dynamic LoRA
autores: H. Zhang; Q. Yan; W. Min; C. Zhang; L. Kuang; Y. Xia
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS)
keywords: Codes; Fuses; Web services; Large language models; Heuristic algorithms; Computer bugs; Maintenance engineering; Genetics; Software; Indexes; Automatic Program Repair; Project-level Patch Generation; Large Language Models; Genetic Algorithm; Dy-namic LoRA
abstract: Automated Program Repair (APR) aims to automate the patch generation for buggy code and is vital in software devel-opment and maintenance. While large language models (LLMs) excel in various tasks, our empirical study shows they still face challenges in APR. LLMs take infilling templates with different qualities as input, and low-quality templates may misguide LLMs in constantly generating incorrect patches. Additionally, LLMs lack project-specific knowledge and struggle to leverage bug context fully. Therefore, we propose EvoAPR, which integrates the genetic algorithm and dynamic LoRA technique to enhance LLMs for better APR. First, to generate high-quality infilling templates, buggy codes are encoded to genetic representations, and genetic operators and multi-angle evaluation are designed to produce better templates. Then, to effectively utilize bug context, a bug-context-aware LoRA fine-tuning method is proposed to fuse various bug contexts by dynamically activating certain blocks of the LoRA module according to the bug index. Finally, these high-quality infilling templates are fed the fine-tuned LLMs for patch generation. Experimental results demonstrate that EvoAPR significantly improves LLMs' performance, surpassing state-of-the-art methods.

titulo: Systematic Review of Fine-tuning Approaches for Large Language Models in the Context of Sinhala
autores: S. Hansaka; D. Sumanathilaka
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Advanced Research in Computing (ICARC)
keywords: Translation; Large language models; Transfer learning; Collaboration; Linguistics; Data augmentation; Natural language processing; Tuning; Systematic literature review; Synthetic data; large language models; low-resource language; cross-lingual transfer; Fine-tuning; parameter-efficient fine-tuning; adapters; data augmentation
abstract: The rapid development of large language models (LLMs) such as GPT-3, GPT-4, LlaMA, and mBERT has significantly advanced the natural language processing (NLP) field across many widely spoken languages. However, the effectiveness of these LLMs on low-resource languages such as Sinhala remained unexplored. With the scarcity of high-quality data and linguistic resources, fine-tuning LLMs in Sinhala has gained significant challenges. With a focus on Sinhala specifically, this systematic review addresses the methodologies and outcomes of adapting large language models for underrepresented languages. The purpose of this review is to synthesize existing research, identify effective strategies, contributions, and improvements, and highlight the challenges and opportunities in this domain. By analyzing various approaches, including data augmentation, transfer learning, cross-lingual transfer, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, adapter tuning, and model adaptation likewise, this review provides a comprehensive and precise idea of the current state of LLM fine-tuning on low-resource languages like Sinhala. The results highlight the importance of using creative methods and collaboration to improve LLM performance and usefulness in linguistic environments with limited resources.

titulo: Quantization-Induced Accuracy Degradation in Small Language Models: A Parametric Scaling Analysis
autores: P. Tripathi; A. Sharma; H. Sharma; V. Singh
venue: 2026 16th International Conference on Advanced Computer Information Technologies (ACIT)
keywords: Modeling; Quantization (signal); Accuracy; Memory; Cognition; Cognitive systems; Law; Training; Degradation; Hardware; Apple Silicon; Edge Deployment; GPT-Generated Unified Format (GGUF); Inference Efficiency; Large Language Models (LLMs); Post-Training Quantization (PTQ); Scaling Laws; Small Language Models (SLMs)
abstract: Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) enables the deployment of large language models (LLMs) on resourceconstrained edge devices, yet the accuracy-efficiency trade-off for Small Language Models (SLMs, 3 B parameters) remains poorly characterized. In this study, we present a systematic empirical study of quantization effects across the Qwen2.5-Instruct model family (0.5 B, 1.5 B, 3 B) at five GPT-Generated Unified Format (GGUF) precision levels (8-bit to 3-bit) on Apple M3 hardware with Metal GPU acceleration. On evaluating 15 model-quantization configurations on two benchmarks: a.) GSM8K (mathematical reasoning) and b.) ARC-Challenge (science reasoning), we obtain 30 controlled data points. We propose and validate a novel parametric scaling law, $A(P, Q, C)=\alpha \ln (P)+\beta\left(1 e^{-\gamma Q}\right)+\delta C+\epsilon$, which jointly models accuracy as a function of parameter count $P$, quantization bit-width $Q$, and task complexity $C$, achieving effective $\boldsymbol{R}^{\mathbf{2}}=\mathbf{0. 9 2 9}$ with a Leave- One-Out Cross-Validation Mean Absolute Error (LOOCV MAE) of 4.4 percentage points. Our analysis reveals that Q4_K_M preserves accuracy within 1-3 percentage points (pp) of the 8-bit baseline while halving memory; 3-bit quantization causes catastrophic degradation on multi-step reasoning (21 pp) yet remains resilient on classification (3.5 pp); and an ablation confirms degradation is largely task-independent $\left(\boldsymbol{\Delta} \boldsymbol{R}^{\mathbf{2}}=\mathbf{0. 0 0 3}\right)$. We identify 3B-Q4_KM (2 GB, 82.5% accuracy, 26 tok/s) as the Pareto-optimal configuration for fanless edge deployment.

titulo: Investigating the Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Indonesian Sentiment Analysis
autores: A. Y. Indrarahmana; P. Janyoi; P. Seresangtakul; S. Kongyoung
venue: 2025 29th International Computer Science and Engineering Conference (ICSEC)
keywords: Computer science; Sentiment analysis; Accuracy; Protocols; Reviews; Large language models; Zero shot learning; Market research; Robustness; Testing; Sentiment analysis; Indonesian; Large Language Models; LoRA; Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning; Zero-shot learning; macro-F1; latency
abstract: Sentiment analysis of user reviews is vital for product evaluation, yet the behavior of large language models (LLMs) in lower-resource languages such as Indonesian remains under-explored. We compare three LLM families (Gemma, Llama, Qwen) against classic RNN baselines (Bi-LSTM, Bi-GRU) on a three-class Indonesian app-review dataset (InfoBMKG, 8,000 reviews) under two settings: zero-shot and LoRA fine-tuning. In the zero-shot setting, a domain-trained Bi-LSTM outperforms all LLMs (macro-F1 0.84), indicating that general pre-training alone is insufficient for this domain. After LoRA fine-tuning, all LLMs improve substantially; Gemma3-4B-it attains an Accuracy of 0.92 and a macro-F1 score of 0.89. Paired, stratified bootstrap testing (B is 10,000; two-sided) with Holm–Bonferroni correction shows that only Gemma3-4B-it achieves a statistically significant macro-F1 gain over Bi-LSTM, while other LLMs exhibit positive but non-significant trends. Despite these gains, Bi-LSTM remains more than 70 times faster under a unified inference protocol, underscoring a practical accuracy-latency trade-off. Overall, LLMs are not uniformly superior to classic deep learning models in this setting; parameter-efficient fine-tuning is key to unlocking LLM performance for Indonesian sentiment analysis. However, deployment choices should balance accuracy targets with latency budgets.

titulo: A Comprehensive Study on Quantization Techniques for Large Language Models
autores: J. Lang; Z. Guo; S. Huang
venue: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, and Communication (ICAIRC)
keywords: Performance evaluation; Quantization (signal); Machine learning algorithms; Reviews; Computational modeling; Large language models; Machine learning; Transformers; Internet of Things; Robots; Machine Learning; Artificial Intelligence; Large Language Model; Quantization
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been extensively researched and used in both academia and industry since the rise in popularity of the Transformer model, which demonstrates excellent performance in AI. However, the computational demands of LLMs are immense, and the energy resources required to run them are often limited. For instance, popular models like GPT-3, with 175 billion parameters and a storage requirement of 350 GB, present significant challenges for deployment on resource-constrained IoT devices and embedded systems. These systems often lack the computational capacity to handle such large models. Quantization, a technique that reduces the precision of model values to a smaller set of discrete values, offers a promising solution by reducing the size of LLMs and accelerating inference. In this research, we provide a comprehensive analysis of quantization techniques within the machine learning field, with a particular focus on their application to LLMs. We begin by exploring the mathematical theory of quantization, followed by a review of common quantization methods and how they are implemented. Furthermore, we examine several prominent quantization methods applied to LLMs, detailing their algorithms and performance outcomes.

titulo: Comparative Analysis of BERTurk and Gemma Models for Turkish Text Classification by LoRA Fine-Tuning
autores: T. Y. Çiftçioğlu; M. Bilgin
venue: 2025 10th International Conference on Computer Science and Engineering (UBMK)
keywords: Training; Adaptation models; Solid modeling; Accuracy; Reviews; Large language models; Text categorization; Training data; Performance metrics; Data models; Review Classification; BERTurk; Gemma; LoRA; Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
abstract: In this study, a text classification system was developed to automatically classify Turkish user reviews based on their rating labels. Both encoder-based BERTurk models and decoder-based Gemma models were utilized, and parameter efficiency in large language models was achieved by applying the LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) method. The effectiveness of the models was examined with varying sizes of the training dataset. Gemma model achieved 69.80% accuracy and 65.56% F1 score with 10.000 training and 2.000 test samples. The same Gemma model achieved 59% accuracy and 55.45% F1 score with 1.000 training and 200 test samples. BERTurk model achieved 74.13% accuracy and 72.17% F1 score with 100.000 training and 20.000 test samples. Additionally, the BERTurk model achieved 66% accuracy and 54.87% F1 score on 1.000 training and 200 test samples. The results of the experiment indicate that model performance varies based on both model size and training data volume, and BERTurk and Gemma models perform well particularly on large datasets.

titulo: Dual-Phase E-Commerce Consumer Review Summarization Based on Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
autores: Z. Shen; Y. Mao
venue: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Parallel and Distributed Processing with Applications (ISPA)
keywords: Deep learning; Adaptation models; Reviews; Purification; Biological system modeling; Large language models; Computational modeling; Semantics; Feature extraction; Electronic commerce; E-Commerce consumer reviews; Text summarization; Large language model; Fine-Tuning; Summary generation
abstract: Consumers increasingly rely on existing reviews to guide purchasing decisions, yet face significant challenges in extracting actionable insights from vast volumes of unstructured e-commerce feedback. Automated review summarization offers a promising solution, with large language models (LLMs) emerging as powerful tools for this task. This study proposes a dual-phase LLM fine-tuning framework for review summarization, decomposing the process into two phases: (1) pros/cons extraction from individual reviews and (2) summary generation from aggregated features. Leveraging the LoRA adapter, we efficiently adapt Qwen-series LLMs for both phases, achieving domain-specific optimization with minimal computational overhead. Experimental results indicate that LLMs, including Qwen series, demonstrate robust performance in review summarization tasks on review data from Amazon. The Qwen series models adapt well to the dual-phase generation framework, with the 7-billion-parameter variant exhibiting particularly outstanding performance. In Phase I, it achieves significant performance improvements compared to smallerparameter Qwen variants and conventional deep learning models. When integrated with the purification module, this model further delivers optimal effectiveness in Phase II. Moreover, cross-platform validation on multilingual datasets confirms the framework's transferability, when applied to the review dataset from JD.com.

titulo: How Low Can Medical Llms Go? an Empirical Study of Low-Bit Quantization
autores: T. Tasfia; A. K. M. Masum; E. Meyer; F. Cumbo; S. Aygun
venue: 2026 IEEE 19th Dallas Circuits and Systems Conference (DCAS)
keywords: Modeling; Quantization (signal); Printing; Large language models; Question answering (information retrieval); Medical services; Natural language processing; MIMICs; Memory; Accuracy; Energy-efficient inference; GPU acceleration; Hardware-aware quantization; Large Language Models (LLMs); Medical LLMs; Mixed-precision quantization
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently shown very promising results on medical tasks such as clinical question answering, report summarization, and decision support. However, their high computational cost makes them difficult to use on resource-constrained devices. Quantization reduces model size and enables lightweight deployment, yet the impact of low-bit precision on medical language understanding remains underexplored. In this work, we present a systematic empirical study of low-bit quantization for medical LLMs. We evaluate multiple 2-, 3-, and 4-bit quantization techniques across several medical natural language processing (NLP) benchmarks and report their results on task accuracy, model size, and inference efficiency. Our study focuses on evaluating different quantization methods on medical data rather than device-specific deployment; the findings show that medical LLMs can be compressed without significant performance degradation, making them strong candidates for future edge and mobile healthcare applications.

titulo: A Comprehensive Review of Llm Neural Network Enhancements for Advanced Driving Assistance Systems Through Quantization
autores: S. B; N. V; A. G S ME
venue: 2025 International Conference on Advancements in Smart, Secure and Intelligent Computing (ASSIC)
keywords: Deep learning; Quantization (signal); Accuracy; Reviews; Computational modeling; Large language models; Safety; Complexity theory; Advanced driver assistance systems; Autonomous vehicles; Deep learning; Large Language Models; Advanced Driver Assistance Systems; Quantization; Activation Aware Weight Quantization
abstract: Deep learning models, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), have shown high degrees of complexity in recent years and have, therefore, made effective quantization techniques necessary. These are very important for the efficient deployment of models into environments of limited resources in autonomous driving and Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS). Quantization is of paramount importance in the field of ADAS, as accuracy directly relates to safety. More importantly, quantization technique advances do allow the design of safety-critical features with higher accuracy in ADAS, such as the brand new Full Self-Driving technology developed by Tesla, whose processing speeds reach over 100 frames per second and with more than 85 % accuracy. This is a survey paper that covers the latest developments in this particular area of operator quantization, which are Gradient-based Post-Training Quantization (GPTQ), Generalized Gradient Update Framework (GGUF), and Adaptive Weight Quantization (AWQ). While memory could be reduced to a low level, performance is not affected at all. Yet, most of the time, it sacrifices the accuracy of the latest advances in quantization, like PTQ or QAT. We review a plethora of advanced quantization techniques to improve both the performance and efficiency of real-world deep learning models. The aim is to demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness achieved when advanced methods of quantization are applied to improve deep learning models for real applications thereby offering insights into promising research opportunities.

titulo: Large Language Models in Power Systems: A Survey on Applications and Fine-Tuning
autores: B. Sun; Y. Yao; H. Yu; H. Ji; G. Song; H. Wang; P. Li
venue: Chinese Journal of Electrical Engineering
keywords: Modeling; Power systems; Tuning; Printing; Training; Large language models; Optimization; Educational institutions; Measurement; Loading; Large language models (LLMs); power vertical domain; parameter-efficient fine-tuning; specialized LLMs
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are promising tools for knowledge representation, reasoning, and decision-making in industrial sectors. The employment of LLM in power systems is receiving increasing attention, but is still limited by the scarcity of domain-specific data, the absence of unified benchmarks, the complexity of integrating heterogeneous data, and strict physical time-varying constraints. This paper presents a focused survey on the applications and fine-tuning techniques of LLMs within power systems. The taxonomy of LLMs is first introduced, covering general foundation LLMs, industry foundation LLMs, domain-specific LLMs, and vertical scenario LLMs. The discussion then addresses the principles, categories of fine-tuning methods, evaluation metrics, and benchmark datasets that support model adaptation. Finally, the current progress, potential applications, and challenges of specialized LLMs in the power sector are examined, with emphasis on hybrid fine-tuning strategies, multimodal data integration, and deployment frameworks designed to ensure secure and reliable power system operation.

titulo: Aspect-Oriented Opinion Extraction with LoRA Fine-Tuning and Prompt
autores: H. Yanagimoto; I. Kisaku; K. Hashimoto
venue: 2024 17th International Congress on Advanced Applied Informatics (IIAI-AAI-Winter)
keywords: Deep learning; Vocabulary; Accuracy; Reviews; Large language models; Natural language processing; Computational efficiency; Prompt engineering; Informatics; Testing; Large Language Model; Deep Learning; Prompt engineering; Fine-tuning; Natural language processing
abstract: This paper proposes a system for Aspect-Oriented Opinion Pair Extraction (AOPE) by fine-tuning a pre-trained large language model with LoRA and adjusting prompts. AOPE is a task that extracts users' aspects and their opinions from reviews, requiring a deep understanding of text, especially capturing the dependency structures within reviews. Pre-trained large language models have a high capability for text comprehension, so the goal is to utilize this effectively. However, adapting a pre-trained large language model to a specific task is challenging. Fine-tuning demands substantial computational resources, and generating appropriate prompts for each task is a laborious process. Our proposed method uses LoRA to reduce the computational resources needed for fine-tuning and combines prompts to improve performance. Evaluation experiments demonstrated that combining prompts with fine-tuning improved accuracy. While there are some areas where accuracy is lower than traditional methods, the efficiency in computational resources highlights the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

titulo: Domain-Specific Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Power Customer Consultation and Fault Inquiry
autores: S. Xu; L. Zhang; L. Zhu; M. Qin; C. Huang
venue: 2026 International Conference on Science Technology Engineering and Management (ICSTEM)
keywords: Modeling; Safety; Testing; Printing; Large language models; Art; Surveys; Labeling; Tuning; Accuracy; large language model; QLoRA; power customer service; fault inquiry; safety evaluation
abstract: Power utilities increasingly require natural-language interfaces that can explain customer-service rules while recognising fault and safety conditions. This study aims to evaluate whether domain-specific parameter-efficient fine-tuning improves consultation quality and fault-inquiry performance compared with an untuned large language model (LLM) and few-shot prompting. A quantitative, paired experimental design was implemented using a reproducible synthetic corpus of 2,400 power-customer cases distributed across eight consultation and fault categories. After validation, the corpus was divided into 70% training, 15% validation and 15% testing sets, and three conditions were benchmarked: M1 base LLM, M2 few-shot prompting and M3 domain QLoRA. The simulated benchmark showed that M3 achieved 88.89% classification accuracy, a macro F1-score of 0.886 and a BERTScore F1 of 0.893. It also produced 99.07% safety compliance and a 1.39% hallucination rate, while its improvement over M1 was significant under McNemar's test $(\mathrm{p}<0.001)$; blinded expert agreement was strong (weighted kappa $=0.857)$. The results indicate that domain adaptation can materially improve technical relevance and safety-oriented escalation in this task. Utilities should combine QLoRA adaptation with expert-reviewed response policies and continuous monitoring. The proposed pipeline provides a practical basis for customer-service triage and operator decision support, but it should not autonomously control grid assets. The principal limitation is that the reported results are simulation-based and require confirmation using anonymised operational data and a deployed model.

titulo: Fine-Tuning LLM's for Domain-Specific Text Generation in Environments with Limited Resource Capabilities
autores: A. P. Stepanov; Y. A. Shichkina
venue: 2025 VI International Conference on Neural Networks and Neurotechnologies (NeuroNT)
keywords: Training; Reviews; Large language models; Memory management; Optimization; Neurotechnology; Chemicals; Biological neural networks; large language model; domain-specific fine-tuning; parameter efficient fine-tuning
abstract: Despite the recent advances in large language models, problems with generation of domain-specific texts are still exist. For example, medical and chemical texts cannot be created by large language models without previous fine-tuning. Generally, this process consumes good amount of memory and computational resources. To address the issue, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) technique was invented, making it possible to train decent large language model on domain-specific datasets. This paper contains review of several existing fine-tuning methods and results of applying PEFT technique to large language model for MRT medical report generation.

titulo: Re-Imagining Supervised Learning with LLMs: A Technical Evaluation across Frontier, Open, and QLoRA-Fine-Tuned Models
autores: S. Gogineni; C. Yuvaraju; G. Suryanarayana; K. D. Returi; V. M. Mohan; M. N. Rao
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Emerging Computing and Intelligent Technologies (ICoECIT)
keywords: Biomimetics; LoRa; Protocols; Radio communication; Communication systems; HTTP; Data communication; Internet; 5G mobile communication; Radio access networks; Supervised Learning; Large Language Models; Regression; Price Prediction; Amazon Reviews 2023; Quantization; Frontier LLMS; Ensemble Learning
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown impressive generalization across many natural language processing tasks. However, the degree to which they can imitate or exceed classical supervised methods for numerical prediction tasks is less established. This paper presents a systematic metric-based evaluation of frontier, open-source and QLoRA fine-tuned LLMS. The aim is to predict price of the products from text-based descriptions from the Amazon Reviews 2023 dataset, and benchmark against traditional supervised regressors. We develop a rigorous experimental pipeline that incorporates data curation, embedding construction, quantization, and ensemble learning. We compare performance across architectures and number of parameters represented. We assess performance using RMSE, R2 and provide resource-cost metrics in the form of inference latency, memory footprint, and quantization-induced degradation. Our results demonstrate that fine-tuned quantized LLMs outperform traditional regressors while offering substantial reductions in computational cost. This study highlights the potential for hybrid architectures in the future in the context of supervised learning.

titulo: Addressing Activation Outliers in LLMs: A Systematic Review of Post-Training Quantization Techniques
autores: P. Czakó; G. Kertész; S. Szénási
venue: IEEE Access
keywords: Quantization (signal); Computational modeling; Throughput; Arithmetic; Decoding; Adaptation models; Transformers; Systematics; Systematic literature review; Large language models; Activation outliers; efficient inference; large language models (LLMs); model compression; quantization
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed natural language processing, yet their deployment remains challenging due to substantial computational, memory, and energy demands. Post-training quantization has emerged as a key strategy for enabling efficient inference, particularly in resource-constrained settings. This systematic review focuses on weight-activation quantization, with a unique emphasis on the emergent outlier phenomenon in LLM activations. This work evaluates recent techniques that mitigate activation outliers and improve quantization efficiency, distinguishing itself from prior reviews. Using the PRISMA methodology, we examine 52 recent studies to uncover key trends and evaluate the effectiveness of different approaches. By synthesizing insights from these works, this review presents a diverse set of techniques and their implications for activation quantization, laying the groundwork for future research and practical advancements in LLM deployment.

titulo: Federated Learning Strategies for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models: A Systematic Literature Review
autores: A. Akhmetov; M. A. Ala’anzy; A. Ibraheem
venue: 2026 11th International Conference on Information and Network Technologies (ICINT)
keywords: Federated learning; Modeling; Large language models; Tuning; Printing; Privacy; Quantization (signal); LoRa; Reviews; Differential privacy; Federated Learning; Large Language Models; Fine-Tuning; Privacy; PEFT; Edge Computing
abstract: Recently, the advancement in natural language processing has been driven by the concept of Large Language Models (LLMs). Nevertheless, the deployment of these models in distributed systems is associated with an essential trade-off in terms of privacy and model performance. This systematic review examines the various methods of federated learning in fine-tuning LLMs that were developed between 2023 and 2025, considering the trade-offs in terms of privacy and performance. The results indicate that the methods of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) have been successful in reducing the bandwidth requirements, while system heterogeneity is the key challenge. In the near future, the research in the area of fine-tuning LLMs needs to be focused on architectural flexibility to suit the constraints of edge devices.

titulo: Instruction Fine-Tuning Optimization for Large Language Models in Power Customer Service Question Answering Systems
autores: H. Xu; Z. Li; P. Liang; Y. Hu
venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Power Engineering (ICPE)
keywords: Adaptation models; Accuracy; Customer services; Large language models; Semantics; Training data; Cognition; Question answering (information retrieval); Tuning; Business; electric power customer service Q&A; large language model; instruction tuning; prompt design; LoRA
abstract: The intelligent upgrade of power customer service systems places higher demands on natural language understanding, while general large language models (LLMs) often perform poorly in specific vertical field question answering (Q&A) tasks due to a lack of structured instruction data. To address this issue, this article proposes a large model instruction tuning method called EIPT (Electricity Instruction Prompt Tuning) for power customer service scenarios to improve the model's adaptability and accuracy in industry Q&A tasks. First, we design prompt templates with business logic based on multi-round question-and-answer business processes and typical customer service task corpora, and build a high-quality instruction set through a combination of automatic generation and expert review. Second, we introduce a task distribution balancing mechanism and use small sample clustering and interclass difference analysis to control the coverage of the training data. Finally, we adopt a low-rank adaptation (LoRA) parameter fine-tuning method to enhance model response consistency and inference accuracy while reducing costs. Experimental results on a power customer service question-answering dataset demonstrate that EIPT achieves significant improvements over unoptimized models in terms of answer quality, semantic matching, and execution stability, validating its feasibility and effectiveness in vertical-domain intelligent customer service systems.

titulo: Smaller Models, Unexpected Costs: Trade-offs in LLM Quantization for Automated Program Repair
autores: F. Vallecillos-Ruiz; G. D’Aloisio; M. Hort; L. Traini; A. Di Marco; L. Moonen
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Software Maintenance and Evolution (ICSME)
keywords: Color; Memory; Modeling; Quantization (signal); Printing; Timing; Energy consumption; Large language models; Maintenance engineering; Measurement; quantization; memory; energy; large language models; automated program repair; empirical study
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are powerful tools and have been increasingly adopted for complex software engineering tasks. As the number of parameters increases, results can often be improved, but this also imposes substantial memory requirements. While quantization effectively reduces the memory footprint, its overall impact is often summarized only by benchmark scores, which mask changes in model behavior and non-functional overheads. In this work, we conduct an empirical evaluation of LLM quantization using Automated Program Repair (APR), a complex task in software engineering. We analyze 13 quantization configurations spanning different bit-widths, methods, and target components (weights and KV-cache) across six representative LLMs, evaluated on two APR benchmarks (HumanEval-Java and Defects4J).Our findings reveal that base and quantized models can provide different sets of repaired problems with little overlap, while retaining a comparable number of repaired problems. Although quantization successfully reduces memory footprints by up to 85%, it increases both inference time and energy consumption, which we attribute to suboptimal hardware utilization. Our Pareto trade-off analysis shows that 48% of the configurations evaluated are strictly dominated by alternatives. Rather than identifying a superior quantization method, our findings highlight that the trade-offs between effectiveness, memory footprint, and energy efficiency are sensitive to the underlying model architecture and the complexity of the task.

titulo: Quantization Undoes Alignment: Bias Emergence in Compressed LLMs Across Models and Precision Levels
autores: P. K. Rath; R. Maliakkal
venue: 2026 IEEE Cloud Summit
keywords: Modeling; Quantization (signal); Printing; Measurement; Large language models; Training; Aggregates; Safety; Tuning; Calibration; large language models; quantization; bias amplification; model compression; fairness; post-training quantization
abstract: Large Language models are routinely compressed via post-training quantization to reduce inference costs and memory footprint for cloud and edge deployment, yet the impact of this compression on model quality remains poorly understood. Existing studies typically compare only two conditions (full-precision vs. a single quantized variant), rely on aggregate bias metrics, and evaluate a single model family, making it impossible to distinguish gradual degradation from threshold-dependent safety failures. We conduct a controlled empirical study of three instruction-tuned models (Qwen2.5-7B, Mistral-7B, Phi-3.5-mini) at five precision levels (BF16 through 3-bit) on 12,148 BBQ bias benchmark items across 5 random seeds, totaling 911,100 inference records. Our results reveal that 3-bit quantization causes 6–21% of previously unbiased items to develop new stereotypical behaviors, following a clear dose-response pattern confirmed via logistic regression, while models’ willingness to select "unknown" answers declines by 17.4%. Crucially, these item-level changes are invisible to standard quality metrics: perplexity increases by less than 0.5% at 8-bit and under 3% at 4-bit across all three models, yet 2.5–5.6% of items already develop new biases at 4-bit. These findings demonstrate that aggregate evaluation metrics systematically miss fairness-critical degradation, underscoring the need for quality-aware compression protocols that explicitly test for bias emergence before deployment.

titulo: A Proposed Model for Arabic Fake Reviews Detection using Fine-Tuned BERT and LLMs
autores: S. A. Salah; M. Waleed Fakhr; A. Dahroug
venue: 2026 ICEENG International Conference for Innovations in Intelligent Computing and Cybersecurity (IICC)
keywords: Modeling; Fake news; Reviews; Few shot learning; Accuracy; Signal detection; Tuning; Labeling; Large language models; Testing; Arabic fake review detection; MARBERT; CAMELBERT; large language models; few-shot learning; QLoRA; text classification
abstract: Fake reviews influence consumer trust and purchasing decisions. The identification of fake reviews is thus important for online shops. Contrast with English where much work has been done there is limited work on fake reviews detection for Arabic. Wide-ranging datasets are currently not widely available. This paper presents the development and evaluation of several models to detect Arabic fake reviews. We optimize several linguistic models like LLaMA-v2 and ALLAM. We subsequently compare their results withBERT-based models, namely CamelBERT and MARBERT. The models received training and testing on the combination of real and synthetic reviews within the framework of Arabic datasets consisting of AFRD, as well as Arabic translated versions of respective Amazon and Yelp reviews datasets. For each tested methodology, the evaluation of the model was carried out using configurations comprising Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score. Our few-shot experiment in this paper for GPT-5.0, DeepSeek, and Gemini is done using five examples from each class. The goal is to test the expert models for generalization on respective datasets of Amazon, Yelp, and AFRD. The performance results for few-shot show an accuracy score of 74%, 64% and 35% on Amazon, Yelp and AFRD respectively along with P, R, F1 vales. The fine-tuned BERT models outperform all aforementioned LLMs on all datasets as per the experimental results.

titulo: Automated Legal Question Answering Using Large Language Models: Fine-Tuned Versus Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Llama and RoBERTa
autores: R. Sthapit; M. Dabbagh; M. Jaddoa
venue: 2026 International Conference on Cybersecurity and AI-Based Systems (Cyber-AI)
keywords: Modeling; Retrieval augmented generation; Tuning; Printing; Grounding; Training; Context; Question answering (information retrieval); Ranking (statistics); Artificial intelligence; fine-tuning; large language models; legal question answering; Llama; retrieval-augmented generation; RoBERTa
abstract: Legal question answering requires accurate, and contextually relevant answers to questions about statutes, regulations and case law. Large language models can produce fluent answers to legal questions but face challenges in understanding complex legal reasoning. So, to enhance the ability to answer legal questions accurately, we have conducted an empirical study of two adaptation methods, fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), across two architecturally distinct open-source models: the generative Llama 3.2-3B Instruct and the extractive RoBERTa-base-squad2. Four systems (fine-tuned Llama, fine-tuned RoBERTa, Llama RAG and RoBERTa RAG) are implemented on the Open Australian Legal QA dataset. We have evaluated the performance of these systems based on answer quality (Token F1, BERTScore F1, ROUGE, METEOR), grounding (faithfulness and hallucination rate) and retrieval quality. Fine-tuned Llama produced the highest answer quality (Token F1 0.6033, BERTScore F1 0.9444) while the shared hybrid RAG pipeline, combining lexical and dense retrieval with cross-encoder reranking, achieved near-ceiling document recall (Recall@3 0.9887), indicating that the reader rather than retrieval limits end-to-end quality. Generative Llama consistently outperformed extractive RoBERTa under both adaptation methods. All experiments executed on a single 16 GB academic GPU using parameter-efficient techniques.

titulo: An Empirical Study of Synthetic Data Augmentation for Few-Shot Text Classification Using Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Ultra-Lightweight Language Model
autores: A. B. H. Jaumeer; V. Ramnarain-Seetohul
venue: 2026 International Conference on Next Generation Computing Applications (NextComp)
keywords: Modeling; Few shot learning; Printing; Accuracy; Training; Labeling; Back; Translation; Synthetic data; Tuning; Few-Shot Learning; Synthetic Data; Back-Translation; Paraphrasing; Large Language Models
abstract: Labelled data scarcity remains a persistent bottleneck in machine learning, particularly when annotation is costly or impractical. Few-shot learning (FSL) addresses this limitation by enabling models to learn fromonly a few examples, analogous to the human ability to generalise from limited exposure. This research aims to find out whether synthetic data generation techniques, namely back-translation and rule-based paraphrasing, can aid few-shot learning of text classification tasks through parameter-efficient fine-tuning using ultralightweight open-source language models. We assessed Microsoft's Phi-2 (2.7B parameters) and Alibaba's Qwen-1.8B with a structured experimental framework using progressively larger subsets of the AG News dataset. The starting point of our assessments is 20 samples (5 per class), which we progressively augment to 40, 60, and 80 samples. The only constant in our experiments is the fixed-sized test set of 200 samples (50 per class). According to the results, both augmentation methods yield a significant performance boost. Phi-2 with backtranslation achieved 84% accuracy at Round 4, an increase of 0.24 from its baseline of 60%, and came within just 2% of its full-data ceiling (86%) using only 20 original samples. Phi-2 back-translation (69%) outperformed its baseline on existing data (63%) at 40 samples, indicating the potential of synthetic data in extremely low-resource settings. Results showed that Qwen-1.8B performed better with paraphrasing, yielding an accuracy of 83%. The best augmentation approach differs by model due to differing pre-training objectives. This research demonstrates that combining synthetic data with parameterefficient fine-tuning of ultra-lightweight models can meaningfully boost few-shot learning performance in low-resource settings.

titulo: Toward Reliable Higher-Order MCQ Generation with Large Language Models: Prompting, Fine-Tuning, and Bias-Aware Evaluation
autores: A. Kumar; A. Mary Chacko
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Recent Advances in Electronics, Communication, Computing, Automation and Power (RECCAP)
keywords: Modeling; Tuning; Cognition; Large language models; Cognitive systems; Chatbots; Taxonomy; Manuals; Retrieval augmented generation; Automated Question Generation; Bloom’s Taxonomy; Higher-Order Cognitive Skills; Large Language Models; Prompt Engineering; MCQ Generation; Educational Assessment; Fine-Tuning; Pedagogic Evaluation
abstract: Automatic generation of multiple-choice questions (MCQs) that assess higher-order cognitive skills in Bloom’s taxonomy remains challenging despite advances in large language models (LLMs).
