This paper presents a systematic study of higher-order MCQ generation using a fixed, literature-validated Chain-of-Thought prompt strategy (PS4) across proprietary and open-source LLMs. Two proprietary models and a parameter-efficient fine-tuned open-source LLaMA model are evaluated under identical prompting conditions. To enable reliable assessment, we propose a Hierarchical Bloom-Aware Evaluation Framework (HBEF) that integrates linguistic validation, pedagogical quality checks, and explicit verification of Analyze-level cognition, supported by both independent LLM-based evaluators and human expert review. Experiments on 260 MCQs show that PS4 reliably enforces linguistic quality and pedagogical validity across models, while higher-order cognitive alignment remains strongly dependent on model capacity. Fine-tuning significantly improves higher-order alignment and distractor quality in the open-source model relative to its base version but does not fully bridge the gap with large proprietary models. The results further reveal evaluator variability and self-evaluation bias in automated assessment, underscoring the need for bias-aware evaluation. Overall, the study highlights the complementary roles of structured prompting, model capacity, fine-tuning, and expert validation in reliable higher-order MCQ generation.

titulo: Adversarial Robustness of LoRA Under Cross-Domain Shift in Indonesian Ride-Hailing Reviews
autores: G. E. Simanjuntak; K. S. Nugroho; M. Isnan; B. Pardamean
venue: 2026 13th Electrical Power, Electronics, Communications, Controls and Informatics Seminar (EECCIS)
keywords: Modeling; LoRa; Robustness; Tuning; Training; Ride hailing; Printing; Reviews; Equations; Ranking (statistics); Adversarial Robustness; Indonesian NLP; LoRA; PEFT; Linguistic Data Security; Subjectivity Detection
abstract: Deploying large language models for subjectivity detection in Indonesian ride-hailing reviews presents substantial challenges due to high linguistic variability and security risks in efficiency-constrained environments. Despite growing adoption of parameter-efficient adaptation methods, their robustness under cross-domain and adversarial conditions remains insufficiently examined. This study aims to investigate the trade-off between adversarial robustness and parameter efficiency by comparing Full Fine-Tuning and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) under a Leave-One-App-Out (LOAO) evaluation framework across Indonesian ride-hailing review datasets from Gojek, Grab, and Maxim. Model resilience is assessed against character-level evasion attacks, including dot insertion and phonetic obfuscation, which exploit the subword tokenization behavior of IndoBERTweet. The key contributions of this study are threefold: (1) empirical evidence that LoRA achieves an average F1-macro of 0.739 while reducing trainable parameters by 97.6%; (2) demonstration that LoRA maintains greater adversarial stability, achieving a robustness gap as low as − 0.79% compared to higher degradation under Full Fine-Tuning; and (3) backdoor resistance analysis showing competitive resilience under training-time compromise scenarios. These findings provide actionable insights into the interactions among linguistic variability, efficiency constraints, and adversarial risk, supporting the deployment of reliable subjectivity-detection systems on Indonesian ride-hailing platforms.

titulo: Resource-Efficient Semantic Retrieval Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using FAISS, Milvus, HNSW, and Product Quantization
autores: A. Rizal; J. T. Wang; G. W. Tanubrata; R. Soeputra; D. Fernando
venue: 2026 International Conference on Mobile, Military, Maritime IT Convergence (ICMIC)
keywords: Indexing; Indexes; Memory; Retrieval augmented generation; Modeling; Vectors; Optimization; Quantization (signal); Information rates; Throughput; Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG); vector database; HNSW; product quantization; FAISS; Milvus; approximate nearest neighbor
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances large language models (LLMs) by integrating external knowledge, but its performance depends heavily on efficient semantic vector search. This paper presents a deployment-oriented empirical study that systematically compares established backends and ANN configurations under a single, controlled RAG pipeline. Specifically, it evaluates FAISS and Milvus using Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs and Product Quantization (PQ), combined with optimized chunking, embedding generation, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction, retrieval, re-ranking, and LLM-based generation. Experiments on Natural Questions and TriviaQA show that optimized indexing reduces retrieval latency by 52.4%-79.6%, increases throughput by up to 230%, and reduces memory usage by up to 40%, while maintaining competitive answer quality (F1: 0.88-0.99). These results demonstrate that vector indexing configuration is a critical design factor for efficient and practical RAG deployment.

titulo: Leveraging Fine-Tuned LLMs, RAG and ReACT for Enhanced Academic Document Analysis and Automated Research Proposal Generation
autores: A. H. Iskandar; E. A. K. Zaman; A. M. Ali; F. S. M. Rashid
venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Sciences (AiDAS)
keywords: Adaptation models; Technological innovation; Text analysis; Accuracy; Large language models; Retrieval augmented generation; Pipelines; Information retrieval; Proposals; Systematic literature review; Large Language Model; Retrieval-AugmentedGeneration; Fine-Tuning; Literature Review Automation
abstract: The accelerating growth of scientific literature presents significant challenges for researchers aiming to synthesize information effectively and identify novel research directions. Conventional Large Language Models (LLMs), while versatile, often lack the nuanced understanding of domain-specific academic structures requisite for optimal contextual retrieval. This paper introduces a fine-tuned framework of Large Language Model (LLM)-based research assistant, developed to enhance literature analysis for automated proposal generation within academic domains. The system employs a structured document ingestion pipeline, incorporating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a reranker module to optimize context relevance and reduce hallucinations. Our RAG approach employs a two-step retrieval process, using cosine similarity followed by a reranker to pinpoint the most relevant documents. It integrates multimodal capabilities through vision-language models for diagram interpretation and ReACT to leverage structured prompt templates for research proposals by analyzing “Limitations” and “Future Work” sections. Our experiments clearly show the value of the reranker where it significantly boosts answer relevancy with an average score of 0.994 post-reranking and frequently guiding the system to achieve perfect rank (1.0000). Crucially, our domain-specific fine-tuning of the language models, employing techniques like LoRA, proved effective in adapting the model to academic discourse, achieving a validation perplexity as low as 1.1716. This signifies enhanced model understanding and specialization, leading to more accurate contextual interpretation, better synthesis of complex ideas, and more coherent proposal generation. The proposed model highlights the effective application of domain-specific fine-tuning to streamline data-driven academic workflows in AI-supported research environments.

titulo: Predicting Fall Risk in Community-Dwelling Older Adults Using a Fine-Tuned Quantized Large Language Model
autores: S. S. Band; F. A. Hampa; F. Gholamrezaie; H. -S. Chen; K. -C. Chang; H. -W. Liang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering
keywords: Older adults; Accuracy; Classification algorithms; Hospitals; Feature extraction; Training; Adaptation models; Data models; Predictive models; Prediction algorithms; Fall prediction; geriatrics; machine learning algorithms; wearable sensors
abstract: Computerized posturography has been employed to quantify an individual’s intrinsic balance control under varying stances, thereby presenting the potential to support autonomous and ambulatory fall risk assessment when integrated with machine learning (ML) techniques. However, the superiority of posturography-based approaches over conventional methods such as questionnaires or physical performance tests remain insufficiently documented. In this study, we compared the predictive performance of various combinations of input data and introduced a novel ML approach that incorporates a Large Language Model (LLM) to enhance prediction while enabling feature-based, summarized explanations to improve the transparency of the predictions. We followed 206 community-dwelling older adults over a 6-month period to monitor fall events. At baseline, all participants completed a survey capturing demographic information, self-reported questionnaires, various physical performance tests, and four standing tasks assessed via tracker-based posturography. The predictive validity of these data in distinguishing fallers from non-fallers was evaluated using traditional ML models, and an LLM enhanced with Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA). The 6-month fall incidence was 16.9%. Traditional ML models achieved an area under the curve (AUC) ranging from 0.54 to 0.71 using different combinations of questionnaire responses, physical performance data, and posturographic parameters. Notably, a higher AUC (0.88) and accuracy (0.86) were achieved by applying the LLM with QLoRA to posturographic parameters alone. In conclusion, this study contributes to a deeper understanding of the relationship between postural control and fall risk, and demonstrates the potential of LLMs to improve predictive accuracy while minimizing the need for labor-intensive expert annotation.

titulo: Advancing Sentiment Analysis for Low-Resource Languages Using Fine-Tuned LLMs: A Case Study of Customer Reviews in Turkish Language
autores: R. S. Kiziltepe; E. Ezin; Ö. Yentür; A. M. Basbrain; M. Karakus
venue: IEEE Access
keywords: Sentiment analysis; Reviews; Adaptation models; Natural language processing; Lexicon; Accuracy; Stars; Analytical models; Transformers; Social networking (online); Machine learning; natural language processing; large language models; sentiment analysis; low-resource languages; Turkish language
abstract: This study investigates the application of advanced fine-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) for Turkish Sentiment Analysis (SA), focusing on e-commerce product reviews. Our research utilizes four open-source Turkish SA datasets: Turkish Sentiment Analysis version 1 (TRSAv1), Vitamins and Supplements Customer Review (VSCR), Turkish Sentiment Analysis Dataset (TSAD), and TR Customer Review (TRCR). While these datasets were initially labeled based on star ratings, we implemented a comprehensive relabeling process using state-of-the-art LLMs to enhance data quality. To ensure reliable annotations, we first conducted a comparative analysis of different LLMs using the Cohen’s Kappa agreement metric, which led to the selection of ChatGPT-4o-mini as the best-performing model for dataset annotation. Our methodology then focuses on evaluating the SA capabilities of leading instruction-tuned LLMs through a comparative analysis of zero-shot models and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuned LlaMA-3.2-1B-IT and Gemma-2-2B-IT models. Evaluations were conducted on both in-domain and out-domain test sets derived from the original star-ratings-based labels and the newly generated GPT labels. The results demonstrate that our fine-tuned models outperformed leading commercial LLMs by 6% in both in-domain and out-domain evaluations. Notably, models fine-tuned on GPT-generated labels achieved superior performance, with in-domain and out-domain F1-scores reaching 0.912 and 0.9184, respectively. These findings underscore the transformative potential of combining LLM relabeling with LoRA fine-tuning for optimizing SA, demonstrating robust performance across diverse datasets and domains.

titulo: Enhancing LLMs with LoRA Fine-Tuning Using Medical Data and Knowledge Graph Enrichment for Improved Healthcare Outcomes
autores: A. Jankov; M. Toshevska; S. Gievska
venue: 2025 MIPRO 48th ICT and Electronics Convention
keywords: Drugs; Training; Ethics; Reviews; Large language models; Medical services; Knowledge graphs; Natural language processing; Medical diagnostic imaging; Context modeling; artificial intelligence; natural language processing; large language models; fine-tuning; medical domain
abstract: This research paper investigates the enhancement of large language models (LLMs) within the medical domain, focusing on members of the Llama family of LLMs. While LLMs have demonstrated remarkable success across various general-purpose natural language processing tasks, their application in specialized domains like medicine is often hindered by limited training on domain-specific data, resulting in suboptimal accuracy and contextual relevance. To address these limitations, this research employs low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to fine-tune LLMs on real-world patientphysician dialogues, effectively capturing the intricacies of medical discourse. Additionally, the knowledge of the LLM is enriched with the SPOKE knowledge graph, a structured repository of medical domain information, allowing the model to generate outputs that are both contextually and scientifically grounded. The experimental results underscore the transformative impact of this dual approach, demonstrating significant advancements in tasks such as automatic diagnosis generation and personalized drug recommendation. However, this research should be viewed as an exploratory proof of concept. Significant limitations, including the constrained evaluation scope and the critical need for expert clinical validation and thorough ethical review, must be addressed in future work before considering real-world applicability.

titulo: Leveraging Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for Personalized Feedback in Undergraduate Object-Oriented Programming Education
autores: Z. Li; J. Wu; Q. Liu; Q. Sun; J. Li; W. Rong
venue: 2026 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN)
keywords: Modeling; Codes; Printing; Tuning; Design methodology; Measurement units; Large language models; Conferences; Software engineering; Training; Automated Feedback; Education Technology; LoRA Fine-tuning; Object-Oriented Design
abstract: In undergraduate software engineering education, architectural design courses are pivotal for fostering higher-order engineering skills through complex, iterative projects. However, providing effective feedback in these courses remains challenges: traditional static analysis verifies functional correctness but cannot evaluate architectural quality, while manual review is unscalable for large student cohorts. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a generalizable LLM-based feedback framework, named Helper, which integrates three core modules: course-adaptable data preparation; lightweight fine-tuning for general models; and context-aware recommendation generation. This paper also presents a dedicated fine-tuning dataset tailored to the Object-Oriented Design (OOD) course. The Helper’s specific instantiation of the OOD course is named OO-Helper. Experimental validation demonstrates that OO-Helper outperforms general foundation models in modification accuracy and design compliance. Qualitative feedback from students confirms that it can act as an effective pedagogical scaffold. The modular framework enables seamless cross-disciplinary migration with minor adjustments, offering broad practical value for CS education.

titulo: Benchmarking Prompt Engineering Against Fine-Tuning for Multi-Label Vulnerability Detection in Solidity Smart Contracts: An Empirical Study
autores: B. Chachar; J. F. Ferreira; M. Cavazza; P. Ferrara; A. Cortesi
venue: IEEE Access
keywords: Modeling; Labeling; Tuning; Contracts; Testing; Prompt engineering; Training; Smart contracts; Signal detection; Codes; Large language models; prompting strategies; smart contracts; solidity; vulnerability detection
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed for smart contract security, yet a fundamental question remains unresolved for practitioners: when confronted with the realistic, multi-label setting where a single contract may harbor several concurrent vulnerabilities, which deployment strategy is more effective — prompt engineering or fine-tuning? This paper provides a rigorous empirical benchmark to answer that question. We evaluate five prompt engineering strategies (Zero-shot, Chain-of-Thought, Structured Chain-of-Thought, Step-back, and Few-shot) across five state-of-the-art open-source LLMs (7B – 24B parameters), and compare them against the same models fine-tuned with QLoRA on a standardized multi-label dataset of real-world Ethereum contracts. Our benchmark yields three specific, quantified findings. First, the performance gap is large and consistent: the best prompt engineering configuration achieves a macro F1-score of 0.311, while fine-tuned models reach 0.79, a gap that holds across all five model architectures. Second, scale alone did not compensate for the absence of task-specific training in this setting: a 24B-parameter model under the best prompting strategy was outperformed by a 7B fine-tuned model, suggesting that the benefit of scale was not sufficient to close the paradigm gap on this structured multi-label task. Third, advanced reasoning strategies (Chain-of-Thought, Structured CoT, Step-back) provided negligible improvement over the zero-shot baseline for this task, suggesting that the evaluated prompt-only approaches struggled with structured multi-label output requirements rather than with reasoning quality per se. These results hold for the five open-source model architectures, five prompting strategies, and Slither-derived benchmark labels used in this study. These findings provide actionable guidance for researchers and practitioners designing LLM-based security tools for Solidity smart contracts.

titulo: Towards Uncertainty-Aware Low-Bit Quantized LLMs for On-Device Inference
autores: L. Sparrenberg; T. Schneider; T. Deußer; A. Berger; R. Sifa
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
keywords: Economics; Adaptation models; Quantization (signal); Uncertainty; Large language models; Computational modeling; Stochastic processes; Probability distribution; Calibration; Reliability; large language models; LLM; quantization; regression; classification; Qwen; Qwen 2.5; GPT
abstract: Quantizing large language models (LLMs) significantly reduces memory usage and computational requirements, enabling efficient on-device inference. However, aggressive quantization can degrade model performance and exacerbate prediction uncertainty. To address this critical issue, we propose a logits-based calibration strategy where the model is restricted to generating a single token from a limited set of predefined decision tokens. By applying a temperature-scaled softmax directly on the logits corresponding to these tokens, we obtain calibrated and interpretable probability distributions, explicitly circumventing stochastic methods such as top-k sampling by directly leveraging deterministic logit values, revealing subtle behavioral shifts caused by quantization. Using Qwen-2.5 models ranging from 7 B to 72 B parameters at various quantization levels (2, 4, 6 and 8-bit), we evaluate our method across four recently released benchmarks encompassing regression (README++, CompLex-ZH, GIRAI) and classification (DarkBench) tasks. Thus, minimizing the risk of data leakage into pre-training data. Results indicate moderate quantization (4-bit) as optimal, particularly when combined with minimal few-shot prompting, enabling quantized LLMs to closely match or surpass proprietary models such as GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 in certain tasks. Our opensource toolkit facilitates straightforward deployment of reliable, uncertainty-aware quantized LLMs for privacy-preserving, ondevice inference, making them suitable for sensitive settings such as human-subject economic experiments and survey analysis.

titulo: Can Quantized On-Premise LLMs Flag Semantic Inflation in Employee Work Logs? A Privacy-Preserving Decision-Support Workflow
autores: S. Gao; M. Huang
venue: IEEE Access
keywords: Modeling; Quantization (signal); Reviews; Large language models; Training; Vocabulary; Correlation; Labeling; Air gaps; Artificial intelligence; Impression management; large language models; on-premise deployment; organizational behavior; post-training quantization; privacy-preserving computing; semantic alignment; semantic inflation
abstract: Monthly self-reported work logs are a standard instrument in Chinese knowledge-intensive firms, used both as attendance evidence and as inputs to measuring individual contribution. Their textual nature, however, makes them susceptible to “Impression Management” (IM), in which employees may use rhetorical complexity to inflate perceived workload. We refer to this specific phenomenon as Semantic Inflation: the case where a log’s textual volume and complexity are disproportionate to its recognized output. Manual auditing of such logs is labor-intensive and subjective, whereas routing sensitive internal logs to cloud-based Large Language Models (LLMs) is often restricted by enterprise compliance policies. To explore an alternative, we present a privacy-preserving, on-premise inference workflow that uses quantized open-weight LLMs (e.g., Qwen-2.5-7B) on a single consumer-grade GPU (no model training or fine-tuning is performed). We define the Semantic Inflation Rate (SIR), a decision-support indicator that combines a Semantic Deviation Index with log length and leader-approved work hours, to flag logs whose textual elaboration is disproportionate to their recognized output. Using a longitudinal dataset of 8,603 monthly-report entries from a single R&D division of one Chinese technology enterprise (2014–2024), we observe an Inverse Precision Effect: within the Qwen-2.5-7B family, both the 2-bit and 4-bit variants align more closely with leader-approved hours than the 8-bit variant (full-sample Pearson  $R \approx 0.50$ , 0.50, and 0.41 for the 2-, 4-, and 8-bit variants, respectively). A test for differences between dependent correlations indicates that the 2- and 4-bit variants are each significantly better aligned than the 8-bit variant but are statistically indistinguishable from each other, so we summarize the ordering conservatively as Q $2~\approx $  Q4 > Q8. These correlations are moderate. We read them as consistent with information-bottleneck reasoning, namely that aggressive post-training quantization may implicitly attenuate low-density rhetorical content, though the mechanism itself is not demonstrated here. SIR is positioned as a decision-support tool that helps managers triage logs for human review. Practical implications: the workflow is feasible on commodity hardware within an air-gapped network, lower-bit quantization does not necessarily degrade alignment on this task, and SIR can surface candidate outliers for human-in-the-loop review while preserving data sovereignty.

titulo: How Does Quantization Impact Privacy Risk on LLMS for Code?
autores: M. N. Haque; H. Yang; Z. Yang; B. Xu
venue: 2025 2nd IEEE/ACM International Conference on AI-powered Software (AIware)
keywords: Training; Privacy; Data privacy; Adaptation models; Quantization (signal); Codes; Computational modeling; Training data; Data models; Software; quantization; privacy; CodeLLMs; Security and privacy
abstract: Large language models for code (LLMs4Code) rely heavily on massive training data, including sensitive data, such as cloud service credentials of the projects and personal identifiable information of the developers, raising serious privacy concerns. Membership inference (MI) has recently emerged as an effective tool for assessing privacy risk by identifying whether specific data belong to a model's training set. In parallel, model compression techniques, especially quantization, have gained traction for reducing computational costs and enabling the deployment of large models. However, while quantized models still retain knowledge learned from the original training data, it remains unclear whether quantization affects their ability to retain and expose privacy information. Answering this question is of great importance to understanding privacy risks in real-world deployments. In this work, we conduct the first empirical study on how quantization influences task performance and privacy risk simultaneously in LLMs4Code. To do this, we implement widely used quantization techniques (static and dynamic) to four representative model families, namely Pythia, CodeGen, GPT-Neo, and starcoder2. Our results demonstrate that quantization has a significant impact on reducing the privacy risk relative to the original model. We also uncover a positive correlation between task performance and privacy risk, indicating an underlying trade-off. Moreover, we reveal the possibility that quantizing larger models could yield better balance than using full-precision small models. Finally, we demonstrate that these findings generalize across different architectures, model sizes and MI methods, offering practical guidance for safeguarding privacy when deploying compressed LLMs4Code.

titulo: Unlocking Sentiment Analysis Potential for Low-Resource Bangla Language by Fine-Tuning LLaMA Model
autores: Z. Ahmed; S. S. Shanto; A. I. Jony
venue: 2024 27th International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (ICCIT)
keywords: Training; Sentiment analysis; Analytical models; Adaptation models; Accuracy; Text analysis; Reviews; Computational modeling; Large language models; Information technology; Natural Language Processing (NLP); Bangla Sentiment analysis; Large Language Model (LLM); LLaMA; E-commerce
abstract: Sentiment analysis, which involves the identification and assessment of the emotional state of the author, constitutes an integral component within the broader context of text analysis. This approach is crucial since it facilitates a holistic understanding of users’ emotions, perspectives, and preferences. The advent of large language models (LLMs), exemplified by LLaMA, has significantly expanded the accessibility of state-of-the-art model applications, including sentiment analysis. Nevertheless, the potential of LLMs in addressing various sentiment analysis challenges has not been extensively explored. This work explores the feasibility of leveraging LLaMA, a Large Language Model (LLM), for sentiment analysis in Bangla, a low-resource language. A dataset of 1,000 Bangla customer reviews was used to fine-tune the model, achieving an overall accuracy of 89.76%, outperforming existing models such as Bangla-BERT by 1%. The study highlights the use of parameter-efficient fine-tuning techniques (LORA and PEFT) to reduce computational overhead, making it suitable for resource-constrained environments. The findings demonstrate the potential of LLMs in advancing sentiment analysis for low-resource languages.

titulo: Comparative Analysis of Multimodal RAG Deployment Strategies for Medical Image Understanding: API-Based, Local Fine-Tuning, and Hybrid Approaches
autores: K. -C. Yang; H. -T. Chu
venue: 2025 Second International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Medicine, Health and Care (AIxMHC)
keywords: Data privacy; Visualization; Large language models; Retrieval augmented generation; Knowledge based systems; Medical services; Vision language model; Question answering (information retrieval); General Data Protection Regulation; Biomedical imaging; Multimodal RAG; Medical Imaging; Vision Language Models; LoRA; DoRA; API; CLIP; MedCLIP; BiomedCLIP; Local VLM; Hybrid MRAG; Visual Question Answering; Clinical Decision Support; Data Privacy; IRB; HIPAA; GDPR; Healthcare AI; Deployment Strategies; Decision Framework
abstract: The advancement of clinical decision support systems depends on the essential integration of medical images together with their corresponding textual reports. The paradigm of Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) shows promise because it uses external knowledge sources to support Large Language Model (LLM) responses. Recent advances such as MMed-RAG demonstrate up to 43.8% improvement in factual accuracy for medical vision-language tasks. This research investigates three main approaches to implement MRAG for medical image understanding through (1) API-based access to strong general-purpose Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) (e.g., GPT-4V, Gemini), (2) local deployment of Vision Language Models (VLMs) with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (e.g., LoRA, DoRA), and (3) a hybrid method that uses pre-trained embedding models (e.g., CLIP, MedCLIP, BiomedCLIP) for local structured knowledge base retrieval alongside a local VLM for secure context-aware response generation. The evaluation assesses these methods through their documented capabilities and literature-based model efficacy and data privacy aspects for Protected Health Information (PHI) and evaluates their deployment complexity and cost alongside scalability and customizability and latency and transparency and knowledge updatability. Through a conceptual case study and decision framework, we analyze the trade-offs for typical healthcare institutions. The research establishes particular medical use cases which demonstrate the best fit for each approach under strict Institutional Review Board (IRB) regulations and data privacy standards including HIPAA and GDPR. This research establishes a decision framework for healthcare ecosystem MRAG solution selection and implementation to address specific healthcare challenges.

titulo: CrashExpert: Expert-Rationale Supervised Fine-Tuning for Traffic Accident Type Classification in Surveillance Scenes
autores: L. Tian; B. Han; P. Wan; Y. Xu; W. Zhou
venue: 2026 International Conference on Image, Signal Processing and Pattern Recognition (ISPP)
keywords: Modeling; Accidents; Vehicles; Tuning; Labeling; Printing; Pedestrians; Cognition; Cognitive systems; Surveillance; traffic accident classification; multimodal large language model; rationale-augmented fine-tuning; surveillance scene understanding; explainable AI
abstract: Existing vision-based traffic accident analysis methods suffer from limited generalization to long-tail accident types and lack semantic-level explanations for their outputs. This paper proposes CrashExpert, an Expert-Rationale Supervised Fine-Tuning framework built upon multimodal large language models. Given a single surveillance image, CrashExpert pairs visual tokens extracted by Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct with structured expert rationales organized into a six-level reasoning chain (Perception, Category, Pattern, Severity, Cause, Conclusion). A hybrid fine-tuning strategy-full fine-tuning of the projection layer combined with LoRA adaptation of the LLM-enables the model to simultaneously output accident type labels and generate interpretable structured rationales. Experiments on our privately constructed dataset Traffic-Crash-Sight demonstrate that CrashExpert achieves the highest recall on the safetycritical pedestrian-vehicle category (80.49 %) among all compared methods, while uniquely providing readable reasoning traces for post-hoc accident review.

titulo: PEFT-Enabled AI Scaffolding for Adaptive Problem-Based Learning A Systematic Literature Review
autores: Kusnadi; E. Utami; Kusrini; T. Hidayat
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Creative Communication and Innovative Technology (ICCIT)
keywords: Learning (artificial intelligence); Modeling; Artificial intelligence; Printing; Reviews; Feedback; Large language models; Systematic literature review; Tuning; Systematics; PEFT; Scaffolding; Problem-Based Learning; Information Systems; Adaptive Gamification
abstract: Parameter Efficient Fine Tuning offers a computationally viable foundation for Large Language Models to deliver adaptive cognitive scaffolding and real-time feedback in Problem-Based Learning environments. Educational institutions frequently face computational resource constraints and model hallucination risks when attempting to deploy generative models for personalized instruction. This study presents a systematic literature review examining how parameter-efficient model adaptation techniques, particularly Low-Rank Adaptation, support adaptive gamification and cognitive scaffolding within Problem-Based Learning. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, a comprehensive search across Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar identified 1,147 records, from which 45 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2022 and 2025 were selected after applying AMSTAR quality criteria. The synthesized findings reveal that Low-Rank Adaptation tuned models like Llama-3.2 and Mistral-7B outperform traditional baselines in classroom dialogue analysis while reducing hardware overhead. Across the reviewed studies, PEFT-enabled adaptive gamification increased student motivation by up to 35.3 percent, enhanced knowledge retention by 32%, automated 61.7% of instructional content creation, and achieved 93.1% accuracy in mitigating hallucination risks via multi-agent scaffolding. System designers and educators can leverage these open-source adaptation frameworks to implement reliable, resource-efficient adaptive gamification in localized learning management systems.

titulo: Longitudinal Summarization of Mental Health Clinical Notes Using Fine-Tuned LLM and Hybrid RAG
autores: R. Dilip; M. Venugopalan
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Technologies in Computing and Communication (ETCC)
keywords: Modeling; Retrieval augmented generation; Printing; Tuning; Recording; Timing; Large language models; Measurement; Grounding; Natural language processing; Longitudinal Clinical Summarization; Mental Health NLP; Retrieval-Augmented Generation; Weak Supervision; Large Language Models
abstract: The ability to summarise longitudinal psychiatric clinical notes will be vital for timely and informed clinical decisions during multiple hospital admissions, as they will carry important information related to symptom trajectory, treatment response and risk evolution. The unstructured and temporally disjointed nature of these records, however, poses significant problems for manual review and for current automated summarization systems that often handle the process of summarizing individual admissions separately, and potentially produce temporally inconsistent or unsupported information. In this work, a longitudinal clinical summarization framework is presented which integrates the heuristic-based instruction tuning with a Hybrid Retrieper-Augmented Generation (Hybrid RAG) model to enhance factual grounding and temporal consistency. Admission-scoped patient history is built from raw psychiatric notes, and weakly supervised data pairs are created with clinically motivated heuristics, which allows using parameter-efficient finetuning methods such as QLoRA to train a LLM on this data. The multi-stage retrieval pipeline with sparse retrieval, dense semantic retrieval, and cross-encoder re-ranking are used to retrieve the evidence to support the generation of the summary during the inference stage, to guide the generation of the admission-specific summary. The longitudinal psychiatric records are used to evaluate the proposed framework on standard summarization metrics and retrieval and temporal consistency proxy measures. The experimental results show that our model outperforms the fine-tuned model with ROUGE-1 score of 0.5034, ROUGE-2 score of 0.4026 and BERTScore F1 score of 0.8884. The framework also gains a temporal precision proxy score of 1.0000, representing perfect temporal consistency in the retrieval using clinician-annotated temporal correctness as the proxy. The findings suggest that the proposed framework could enhance the reliability of longitudinal psychiatric clinical summarization by providing well-founded facts, structural coherence, and temporal consistency.

titulo: Enhancing Fine-Tuning of LLMs for Domain-Specific Literature Review
autores: M. Xu; T. Xu; X. Zhu; Y. Wang; Y. Zou; C. Wang
venue: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference on Industrial Electronics for Sustainable Energy Systems (IESES)
keywords: Training; Measurement; Adaptation models; Analytical models; Accuracy; Computational modeling; Standards; Optimization; Systematic literature review; Investment
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer transformative capabilities for automating literature reviews in specialized domains such as engineering and new energy research. We present an enhanced approach to fine-tuning a state-of-theart LLM with greater technical depth, emphasizing efficient adaptation techniques, robust data preparation, and optimized training on limited computing resources. Our methodology constructs a domain-specific dataset of literature in the new energy domain and formats it for supervised fine-tuning of a 7 billionparameter open LLM (e.g., LLaMA-7B), using cross-entropy loss minimization as the training objective. We discuss parameterefficient strategies (e.g., LoRA) that drastically reduce trainable parameters while maintaining performance [1], [2]. The model was trained on a multi-GPU setup with memory optimizations to handle the LLMs scale [3]. Quantitative evaluation using standard metrics for language generation-ROUGE for summarization quality and BLEU for content overlap-indicates improved output relevance after fine-tuning. The fine-tuned model demonstrates better recall of domain-specific terminology and produces more concise, informative summaries, reflected in higher ROUGE scores compared to the base model. We also analyze the trade-offs between model performance and computational cost: our fine-tuning approach balances accuracy gains against resource expenditure, ensuring the investment is justified by significant time savings in literature analysis. This work provides a blueprint for efficiently adapting LLMs to specialized research tasks, with implications for scaling AI solutions in scientific knowledge management across various engineering domains.
